findings.title: Command Injection via 'cmd' parameter
findings.description: The 'cmd' GET parameter reflects output of injected shell commands. Evidence: marker 'assurix_cmdi' appeared in response after injecting '; echo assurix_cmdi_1'.
findings.remediation: Never pass user input directly to shell commands. Use parameterized APIs or safe alternatives. If command execution is required, validate and sanitize input strictly, and avoid shell invocation. For Node.js, avoid child_process.exec() and use execFile() or spawn() with arguments array.

findings.title: Redirect at /api to /api/
findings.description: Accessing /api returns a 302 redirect to /api/. This may indicate an API root endpoint.
findings.remediation: Consider returning a 404 or 403 if the API is not meant to be publicly discoverable. Alternatively, ensure proper authentication at the API root.

findings.title: Forbidden response for /.env
findings.description: Accessing /.env returns 403 Forbidden. The finding notes it 'may be bypassable' but no bypass evidence was provided.
findings.remediation: Ensure .env files are not served by the web server. Block all methods to the path. Consider moving sensitive files outside web root.
